messages:
Yuki: New hire stumbled over auth weirdness in the TypeScript sampleapp. Leaving notes here.
Carlos: what happened?
Yuki: They copied the quickstart, ran it in Docker, and sometimes requests 403/401. Turns out envs in the repo examples are inconsistent: .env.sample uses REDWOOD_API_KEY, docker-compose uses REDWOOD_DEV_KEY, and CI templates set REDWOOD_KEY.
Maya: Oof. That explains language parity problems too: different SDKs pick different vars so the same credentials behave differently between Node and Python.
Yuki: Repro steps I used:
```
# local .env
REDWOOD_DEV_KEY=dev_pk_aaa
REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_pk_bbb
# start node sample -> uses REDWOOD_DEV_KEY -> works locally
# run python sample -> picks REDWOOD_API_KEY -> 403 (scope mismatch)
```
Carlos: Is REDWOOD_DEV_KEY a legacy name? I don't recall it in the spec.
authbot: Note: REDWOOD_DEV_KEY introduced in early prototypes; not part of the official env var spec. Deprecation planned pending cleanup.
Maya: Two separate problems: (1) inconsistent examples across artifacts, (2) SDKs need a predictable precedence and clearer error messages when scope mismatch or rotation happens.
Yuki: Short-term fixes suggested:
- Normalize all examples to use REDWOOD_API_KEY only and remove aliases from .env.sample and docker-compose.
- Add a startup diagnostic in sampleapp that prints which env var wins and a non-sensitive hint about scope (e.g., "using REDWOOD_API_KEY (project)" or "using legacy REDWOOD_DEV_KEY").
- On 401/403, SDK should surface a clear hint: \"Auth failed: possible key scope mismatch or rotated key. Check REDWOOD_API_KEY vs legacy envs and REDWOOD_ORG/REDWOOD_PROJECT.\"
Carlos: For streams, also add logic to re-read env vars on reconnect and clear any cached auth header on an auth failure before a single retry. That should mitigate rotation hits.
Maya: Can we also add a tiny debug command `rw auth:inspect` that prints which var will be used and the effective scope without printing the key itself? Could be part of the CLI quickstart.
Yuki: Good idea. New hires spend time guessing which one the runtime used. A one-line inspect output would save minutes.
Docs: I'll file a docs ticket to standardize examples and add a troubleshooting short table for local vs docker vs CI.
authbot: Created ticket DEVX-7832: "quickstart env parity & SDK auth hints" at 3610023488.
Carlos: I'll open a small PR to remove REDWOOD_DEV_KEY from .env.sample and docker-compose, add startup diagnostic, and include a note in README. PR: https://git.example/redwood/sampleapp/pull/812
Maya: I'll follow up with SDK PRs to align env precedence across languages and to clear auth cache on 401 then retry once. Also will add a unit test that simulates a mock rotation.
Yuki: Thanks. Ping me for review. Also can we add a short onboarding blurb: "If you see 403 in one language and not another, check env var aliasing and CI templates." New hires keep hitting this.
Docs: Filed DOCS-421: "Auth env aliases & troubleshooting" referencing DEVX-7832.
Carlos: Nice catch. Hopefully this will cut down the onboarding support noise.
Maya: Agreed. Small changes but big payoff for DX.
